rule: Each call in a multi-line method chain is reported on the line of its own method name, not the chain's first line. | Call on a **computed receiver** (call result, index, literal, `super` when the superclass is not in the scan): `.member` — a leading dot means "receiver unknown".
notes: call_type convention used throughout this corpus: a callee that is a member of a type (`T#m`) or a receiver-qualified guess (`recv.m`, `.m`) is `method`; a free function (`file.f`, `std.x.f`) is `direct`. All files sit directly under src/, so the file qualifier is the basename (`app`, `util`). Each call is on the line of its own `.add`. Only the first has a declared receiver (`b: Builder`); the next two are called on the result of a call that takes an argument → computed receiver `.add`, low.
